name: Tiny Tim Tomato
summary: Tomate cherry micro-enano y determinado, especialmente útil para espacios pequeños. La identidad Tiny Tim está bien corroborada; Garden separa sus datos de variedad de las reglas generales del tomate.

germination.guidance: Treat as a tomato for germination and early seedling care; the purchased variety is Tiny Tim, but Garden should not invent packet-specific germination days until the packet arrives.

thinning.short: Keep one final vigorous plant per compact fruiting position
thinning.guidance: Tiny Tim is compact but still a fruiting tomato. In a small hydro position, preserve the strongest plant rather than maintaining a seedling cluster.

pruning.short: Do not apply indeterminate-tomato pruning automatically
pruning.guidance: Tiny Tim is determinate and micro-dwarf. Avoid aggressive sucker removal by default; prioritize healthy foliage and remove only damaged or clearly problematic growth unless real plant evidence supports more intervention.

harvest.short: Harvest cherry fruit when fully colored and firm
harvest.guidance: Use fruit color and firmness as the primary harvest cues. The ~45-day figure is a variety reference, not a promise for every indoor system.

flowering.short: Flowering and fruit set are expected productive stages
flowering.guidance: Track first flowers and fruit set as canonical events. Do not treat flowering as something to suppress as with leaf herbs.

hydroponics.short: Tomato hydro targets exist at crop level
hydroponics.guidance: OSU lists tomato at EC 2.0–4.0 mS/cm and pH 6.0–6.5. Use as a crop-level reference and respect the limits of the actual compact reservoir/system.

problems.short: Watch fruit load, light, heat and root-space limits
problems.guidance: A compact canopy does not mean a tiny root or nutrient demand. Garden should use actual history and photos to detect support, light or fruit-load issues.

name: Fragrant Dwarf Dianthus Mix
variety: Mini mixed / dwarf fragrant type — packet identity pending
summary: Dianthus compacto de flores mixtas. La compra confirma un tipo mini/mixto, pero Garden mantiene la especie exacta en espera hasta revisar el sobre recibido; Dianthus chinensis se usa solo como contexto, no como identidad canónica.

metrics.label: Hydro pH / EC
metrics.note: Do not map carnation targets to unresolved dwarf mix

germination.guidance: Do not assign a precise germination window until the purchased packet or exact seller evidence resolves the mix. Seed propagation is normal for Dianthus chinensis context.

thinning.short: Thin by vigor after identity and emergence are observed
thinning.guidance: For a compact flowering position, reduce severe crowding while preserving the strongest seedlings. Do not copy outdoor spacing literally.

pruning.short: Deadheading can support repeat bloom in Dianthus context
pruning.guidance: NC State notes deadheading and trimming after heavy bloom for D. chinensis. Apply this only after the actual plant matches that growth pattern; do not assume the purchased mix is D. chinensis yet.

harvest.guidance: Garden should treat this as an ornamental flowering crop, not an edible harvest crop.

flowering.short: Flowering is the primary target stage
flowering.guidance: Track buds, first bloom and bloom cycles. Deadheading decisions should depend on the actual plant and resolved identity.

hydroponics.short: No accepted exact hydro target yet
hydroponics.guidance: OSU has a hydroponic carnation range, but this purchased dwarf Dianthus mix is not confirmed as a carnation cultivar. Garden therefore leaves EC/pH pending rather than collapsing genus and crop type.

problems.guidance: Dianthus chinensis context is susceptible to crown/root problems with poor drainage. In hydro, use this as a caution signal rather than a diagnosis.

name: Mini / Lunchbox-type Sweet Bell Pepper
variety: Mini sweet bell / Lunchbox-type — packet identity pending
summary: Pimiento dulce mini comprado como tipo Lunchbox. Garden no asume que sea la serie propietaria de Johnny's hasta ver el paquete; usa Capsicum annuum y referencias de Lunchbox solo como contexto de cultivo.

metrics.label: Lunchbox context
metrics.note: Johnny's series, not yet packet fact

germination.short: Warm germination; pepper seedlings are slow when cool
germination.guidance: USU recommends warm germination around 80°F for peppers. Johnny's Lunchbox series likewise uses warm seed-starting conditions, but cultivar-specific timing remains pending until the packet is verified.

thinning.short: Keep one strong fruiting plant per compact position
thinning.guidance: Once true leaves establish, retain the strongest seedling in a small hydro position. Outdoor inch spacing is not a pod rule.

pruning.guidance: Preserve enough foliage to support fruit and prevent sun/light stress. Garden should only recommend shaping after seeing the actual plant architecture.

harvest.short: Pick fruit firm; green or fully colored depending goal
harvest.guidance: USU supports harvesting peppers green or fully colored while firm. Johnny's Lunchbox series reaches full-size green before ripe color; use actual purchased fruit color once known.

flowering.short: Protect flower set from temperature stress
flowering.guidance: USU notes poor fruit set under cold nights or very hot days. Track flower drop as an observation before inferring nutrient problems.

hydroponics.short: Pepper hydro targets exist at crop level
hydroponics.guidance: OSU lists peppers at EC 0.8–1.8 mS/cm and pH 5.5–6.0. Treat this as crop-level reference, not an exact cultivar prescription.

problems.short: Watch blossom drop and blossom-end rot signals
problems.guidance: Temperature extremes, irregular moisture and calcium availability are relevant pepper risks. Garden should distinguish observed symptoms from inferred causes.

name: Chinese Light Green Celery
summary: Apio chino de tallos finos y follaje aromático. Fuentes comerciales coinciden en el tipo Light Green pero discrepan entre var. secalinum y var. dulce; Garden conserva Apium graveolens como identidad segura hasta resolver la clasificación del sobre.

germination.short: Celery seed can be slow and uneven
germination.guidance: USU notes celery seed can germinate unevenly and that soaking can help leach natural inhibitors. Do not assign the commercial Light Green timing as a guaranteed packet result before User Zero observes it.

thinning.short: Favor a strong final crown while avoiding early root damage
thinning.guidance: Chinese celery is finer than conventional stalk celery, but a compact position still needs enough crown and root space. Thin severe competition rather than copying field spacing.

pruning.short: Harvest outer stalks; preserve the center
pruning.guidance: Treat maintenance as selective outer-petiole harvest rather than top pruning. Preserve the active inner crown.

harvest.short: Outer stalks can be harvested selectively
harvest.guidance: USU supports removing outer petioles as they size while preserving inner growth. Chinese Light Green references describe thinner stalks/leaves and cut-and-come-again use.

flowering.short: Prolonged cool exposure can trigger bolting
flowering.guidance: USU notes extended cool temperatures can induce flowering in celery. Record a flower stalk as a stage/stress observation, not automatically a nutrient issue.

hydroponics.short: Celery hydro crop reference is available
hydroponics.guidance: OSU lists celery at EC 1.8–2.4 mS/cm and pH 6.5. This is crop-level hydro guidance; the Chinese Light Green subtype may behave differently in a small shared reservoir.

problems.short: Steady moisture and calcium availability matter
problems.guidance: USU identifies water stress as a quality problem and blackheart as a calcium-related disorder. Garden should only diagnose after symptoms and history support it.

name: Tiny Tim Sweet Alyssum
summary: Aliso dulce compacto de flor blanca y fragante. La identidad Lobularia maritima está respaldada tanto por el listing comprado como por Extension; el tamaño exacto Tiny Tim se conserva como evidencia del vendedor.

metrics.label: Seller germination
metrics.note: Purchase listing; not Extension-verified cultivar timing

germination.guidance: The exact purchase listing reports 5–7 day germination. Garden keeps this as seller/manufacturer-level guidance until User Zero provides actual germination evidence.

thinning.short: Thin only enough to prevent severe crowding
thinning.guidance: Sweet alyssum naturally forms a low branching mound. A compact flowering position can retain a small cluster initially, then reduce weak competitors based on real canopy density.

pruning.short: Shear/deadhead after bloom decline to encourage rebloom
pruning.guidance: Extension sources support cutting back sweet alyssum when flowering declines. Avoid cutting into the crown; use actual bloom state as the trigger.

harvest.short: Flowering ornamental; no routine food harvest
harvest.guidance: Garden treats Tiny Tim as a flowering ornamental. Do not generate culinary guidance from unrelated alyssum claims.

flowering.short: Dense fragrant white bloom is the target stage
flowering.guidance: The purchased Tiny Tim listing describes tiny white honey-fragrant flowers. Track first bud, first bloom and rebloom after trimming as useful events.

hydroponics.short: No accepted exact hydro target yet
hydroponics.guidance: Garden has no strong crop-specific hydroponic EC/pH source for Tiny Tim alyssum, so precise targets remain pending.

problems.guidance: Extension references describe sweet alyssum as a cool-season performer and note bloom decline in heat. Use actual indoor temperature and bloom history before intervening.

name: Monterey Strawberry
summary: Cultivar de fresa day-neutral de UC Davis. User Zero compró cinco plantas bare-root, no semillas; Garden debe conservar ese tipo de material y registrar el establecimiento real después de recibirlas.

germination.short: Not applicable — purchased as bare-root plants
germination.guidance: Do not show seed-germination instructions for this inventory item. The relevant first stage is bare-root establishment after arrival.

thinning.guidance: Each bare-root crown is an individual plant. Establish crowns separately and evaluate vigor after transplant rather than thinning seedlings.

pruning.short: Prioritize crown establishment before runner/leaf management
pruning.guidance: Do not prescribe runner removal or aggressive leaf cleanup automatically. Garden should first observe transplant recovery, crown condition and the actual production goal.

harvest.guidance: Monterey is a fruiting day-neutral cultivar. Use actual fruit color and condition rather than a generic days-from-planting promise for bare-root hydro establishment.

flowering.short: Day-neutral flowering is a defining cultivar trait
flowering.guidance: UC Davis identifies Monterey as day-neutral. Track first flowers and fruit set as important real events; Illinois Extension has also evaluated Monterey directly in hydroponic day-neutral production.

hydroponics.short: Direct hydro evidence exists for day-neutral Monterey
hydroponics.guidance: Illinois Extension has grown Monterey hydroponically. OSU lists strawberry at EC 1.8–2.2 mS/cm and pH 6.0; use that as a crop-level reference, not a guarantee for the specific compact machine.

problems.short: Watch transplant establishment and powdery mildew
problems.guidance: UC Davis notes Monterey is susceptible to powdery mildew. Garden should also treat bare-root arrival condition and crown establishment as first-order evidence before diagnosing later decline.

name: Seaside F1 Spinach
summary: Espinaca F1 de hoja lisa, erguida y verde oscura, lenta para espigar y con ventana extendida de baby leaf. Johnny's ofrece una referencia exacta del cultivar; USU aporta el contexto de espinaca para Utah.

germination.guidance: USU reports spinach emergence in about 7–10 days with best germination around 55–65°F and reduced germination above 80°F. Use User Zero's actual Seaside emergence once available.

thinning.short: Thin after true leaves based on final leaf goal
thinning.guidance: USU thins spinach when plants have 3–4 true leaves. In a hydro pod, do not copy field inches literally; preserve enough space for the intended baby-leaf or larger-leaf harvest style.

pruning.short: No shaping prune; harvest leaves while protecting the growing point
pruning.guidance: Spinach is managed by leaf harvest rather than branching cuts. Preserve the basal growing point for repeat harvest.

harvest.short: Baby leaf or repeated larger-leaf harvest
harvest.guidance: Johnny's lists Seaside at about 30 days and an extended baby-leaf window. It supports cutting above the basal plate for cut-and-come-again; USU also supports removing older leaves first while younger leaves continue.

flowering.short: Heat and long days increase bolting risk
flowering.guidance: USU notes warm temperatures and long days promote bolting and bitterness. Seaside is specifically described by Johnny's as slow-bolting, not bolt-proof.

hydroponics.short: Spinach hydro crop targets are available
hydroponics.guidance: OSU lists spinach at EC 1.8–2.3 mS/cm and pH 6.0–7.0. Johnny's does not label Seaside itself as its hydroponic-performer cultivar, so Garden should not add that badge by inference.

problems.short: Heat, bolting and downy mildew are key signals
problems.guidance: Seaside has a documented downy-mildew resistance profile, but resistance is race-specific and not immunity. Garden should never diagnose disease from variety metadata alone.
